Spoodoire|woo:29077.hint: Chromatopelma chromatopelma New World Arboreal new-world-arboreal A web architect of the tarantula world, Chromatopelma cyaneopubescens dazzles with its colours and visibility, thriving in dry, well-ventilated setups.
Spoodoire|woo:29077.name: Chromatopelma cyaneopubescens

Spoodoire|woo:29161.hint: Ceratogyrus ceratogyrus Old World Terrestrial old-world-terrestrial African fossorial with a penchant for deep burrows, webbed entrances and the odd defensive display. Not for beginners, but a rewarding challenge for experienced hands.
Spoodoire|woo:29161.name: Ceratogyrus darlingi

Spoodoire|woo:29175.hint: New World Burrowing new-world-burrowing Nhandu nhandu Struts about like it owns the place, only pausing to flick a hair or redecorate with a modest patch of webbing. Not big on drama, unless it’s dinnertime or you meddle with its hide.
Spoodoire|woo:29175.name: Nhandu coloratovillosus

Spoodoire|woo:29180.hint: Homoeomma homoeomma New World Burrowing new-world-burrowing Unfazed by life’s dramas, this one spends its days rearranging substrate, sulking in a burrow, or pretending dinner is an unexpected audit.
Spoodoire|woo:29180.name: Homoeomma chilensis

Spoodoire|woo:29185.hint: Old World Arboreal old-world-arboreal Pterinochilus pterinochilus Likes to turn the enclosure into a construction site, then sulks behind silk walls whenever you need to check on it.
Spoodoire|woo:29185.name: Pterinochilus murinus RCF

Spoodoire|woo:29187.hint: Chilobrachys chilobrachys Old World Burrowing old-world-burrowing A brisk-growing, fossorial webber from Thailand, best kept by those with a taste for silkwork, burrowing and a spider that keeps you guessing. Not for handling.
Spoodoire|woo:29187.name: Chilobrachys natanicharum

Spoodoire|woo:29190.hint: New World Arboreal new-world-arboreal Psalmopoeus psalmopoeus Masters of acrobatics and dramatic redecorating, P. irminia disappears for days, only to reappear mid-moult or when a cricket dares cross the wrong bit of silk.
Spoodoire|woo:29190.name: Psalmopeus irminia

Spoodoire|woo:29198.hint: Lasiodora lasiodora New World Terrestrial new-world-terrestrial Confident, hefty terrestrial from Brazil; visible, bold, with a healthy appetite. Suits keepers with some tarantula experience who value presence over subtlety.
Spoodoire|woo:29198.name: Lasiodora klugi

Spoodoire|woo:29219.hint: Monocentropus monocentropus Old World Terrestrial old-world-terrestrial Spins enough web to convince you a silk factory’s moved in, then vanishes for days—only reappearing to snatch dinner with unseemly enthusiasm.
Spoodoire|woo:29219.name: Monocentropus balfouri

Spoodoire|woo:29223.hint: Acanthoscurria acanthoscurria New World Terrestrial new-world-terrestrial Bold as brass at feeding time, reserved the rest—shows off its knees with far more enthusiasm than its webbing.
Spoodoire|woo:29223.name: Acanthoscurria geniculata

Spoodoire|woo:29228.hint: New World Burrowing new-world-burrowing Tliltocatl tliltocatl Calm as a cuppa left to cool, occasionally seen loitering at the burrow entrance like it’s contemplating life’s big questions—provided nobody’s poking about with tongs.
Spoodoire|woo:29228.name: Tlitocatl albopilosus

Spoodoire|woo:29230.hint: New World Burrowing new-world-burrowing Phormictopus phormictopus Bold enough to glare at you, hungry enough to lunge at dinner, and not remotely interested in your approval—just mind your fingers at feeding time.
Spoodoire|woo:29230.name: Phormictopus auratus

Spoodoire|woo:29240.hint: Old World Arboreal old-world-arboreal Poecilotheria poecilotheria Expert at lurking unseen until dusk, then appears in a blur just as you’re tidying the enclosure. Not a fan of interruptions or unnecessary drama—webbing reflects current moo
Spoodoire|woo:29240.name: Poecilotheria regalis

Spoodoire|woo:29256.hint: Grammostola grammostola New World Terrestrial new-world-terrestrial Rarely in a hurry, occasionally visible, and only spins webbing where strictly necessary—think of it as the minimalist’s answer to tarantula keeping.
Spoodoire|woo:29256.name: Grammostola pulchra

Spoodoire|woo:29264.hint: Birupes birupes Old World Burrowing old-world-burrowing Usually takes reclusive to dramatic new depths—if you glimpse a flash of blue, consider yourself lucky and assume it’s already retreated with frankly unnecessary haste.
Spoodoire|woo:29264.name: Birupes simoroxigorum

Spoodoire|woo:29328.hint: Caribena caribena New World Arboreal new-world-arboreal Arboreal architect adept at curtain-twitching from elaborate silk tunnels; shows itself mostly at dusk, unless you’re keen to spot the occasional grumpy leg in daylight.
Spoodoire|woo:29328.name: Caribena versicolor

Spoodoire|woo:29330.hint: New World Terrestrial new-world-terrestrial Golden-capped and genuinely relaxed, Brachypelma albiceps is a hardy, long-lived terrestrial tarantula ideal for keepers who prefer slow growth and manageable care.
Spoodoire|woo:29330.name: Brachypelma Albiceps

Spoodoire|woo:29524.hint: Old World Burrowing old-world-burrowing Pterinochilus pterinochilus Builds web tunnels like it’s plotting an escape, then sulks underground until dinner. Approach with respect—this one has no time for indecisive keepers or loose enclosure l
Spoodoire|woo:29524.name: Pterinochilus murinus TCF

Spoodoire|woo:29750.hint: Old World Arboreal old-world-arboreal Poecilotheria poecilotheria Spends most of its time lurking in high-rise silk tunnels, only to bolt up the nearest surface the moment it suspects you’ve come to tidy up its mess.
Spoodoire|woo:29750.name: Poecilotheria metallica

Spoodoire|woo:29814.hint: New World Burrowing new-world-burrowing Pamphobeteus pamphobeteus Has the presence of a tank but the nerve of a napper—mostly seen lurking, unless spooked, in which case it exits stage left with unexpected enthusiasm.
Spoodoire|woo:29814.name: Pamphobeteus sp. “machala”

Spoodoire|woo:29840.hint: Old World Arboreal old-world-arboreal Poecilotheria poecilotheria Prefers to lurk in vertical retreats, flashes a leg at dusk, and relocates at warp speed if you so much as sneeze near the enclosure.
Spoodoire|woo:29840.name: Poecilotheria ornata

Spoodoire|woo:30670.hint: Old World Arboreal old-world-arboreal Poecilotheria poecilotheria Never misses a meal unless plotting a moult, and reliably lurks upside-down just when you’re certain it’s vanished entirely.
Spoodoire|woo:30670.name: Poecilotheria miranda

Spoodoire|woo:30754.hint: Heteroscodra heteroscodra Old World Arboreal old-world-arboreal Highly committed to the art of disappearing, only pausing from web fortress renovations to flatten a cricket or give you a threat pose you didn’t ask for.
Spoodoire|woo:30754.name: Heteroscodra maculata

Spoodoire|woo:30782.hint: Neoholothele neoholothele New World Arboreal new-world-arboreal Quick to vanish behind silk curtains, this one webs like it’s rehearsing for a minor home renovation show and only emerges when it’s convinced you aren’t paying attention.
Spoodoire|woo:30782.name: Neoholothele fasciaaurinigra

Spoodoire|woo:30821.hint: Harpactira harpactira Old World Burrowing old-world-burrowing Thinks it’s a burrowing architect, but spends most evenings lurking by the front door like a blue-legged bouncer waiting for the local takeaway to arrive.
Spoodoire|woo:30821.name: Harpactira pulchripes

Spoodoire|woo:30910.hint: Cyriocosmus cyriocosmus New World Burrowing new-world-burrowing Expects darkness, detests drama—vanishes at the hint of movement but leaves a subtle webbed calling card to prove it hasn’t tunnelled into oblivion just yet.
Spoodoire|woo:30910.name: Cyriocosmus elegans

Spoodoire|woo:30962.hint: Aphonopelma aphonopelma New World Terrestrial new-world-terrestrial Expert at vanishing acts; expect either bold stripy legs on display or nothing but a mysteriously shifting mound of dirt for weeks at a time.
Spoodoire|woo:30962.name: Aphonopelma seemanni

Spoodoire|woo:31136.hint: Davus davus New World Burrowing new-world-burrowing Prone to a sudden moonwalk into the hide at the faintest hint of movement—clearly believes the best offence is making you question if it was ever there at all.
Spoodoire|woo:31136.name: Davus pentaloris
